citations.quote: The success of models like that of Vasicek (1977) and that of Cox, Ingersoll and Ross (1985) was mainly due to their possibility of pricing analytically bonds
Vasicek (1977) assumed that the instantaneous spot rate under the real-world measure evolves as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
When r is high, mean reversion tends to cause it to have a negative drift; when r is low, mean reversion tends to cause it to have a positive drift

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: Short-rate models parameterise the term structure with one stochastic state variable r(t). Vasicek (mean-reverting Gaussian) and CIR (square-root diffusion, non-negative) admit affine bond-price closed forms. Hull-White extends Vasicek with a time-dependent drift theta(t) calibrated to today's curve exactly, making it the practitioner default for path-dependent rate derivatives.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Short-Rate Models
